messages.subject: Re: CODEX 1.6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ted and Nancy,

Yes, I agree with you both that the first two are boundary issues and this will not affect your results. For your third question, the difference is due to how coverage is calculated.Although both methods adopt the mapping equality >=20 in the analysis, CODEX outputs the TOTAL number of reads that cover the exon whereas your samtools + bedtools pipeline calculate PER-BASE coverage and take the MEAN. When calling the CNVs, CODEX has the resolution of exons and we have been using the total coverage. Besides, as you would imagine, the total versus the mean is just by a factor of exonic length, which will be captured by the beta term in CODEX.

BTW, I’m cc’ing our mailing list in case other users have similar questions. Let me know if you want me to have your email address removed from the thread.

Hope that this clarifies,
Yuchao

> On Feb 7, 2017, at 8:59 AM, Zhang, Nancy R <n...@wharton.upenn.edu> wrote:
>
> Dear Ted,
> I will try to answer your questions below. Yuchao, the first author on the paper and the  author of CODEX, is traveling and may want to fill in.
> Nancy
>
> Sent from my iPhone
>
> On Feb 6, 2017, at 7:16 PM, Ted Toal <twt...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
>
> > To whom it may concern,
> >
> > I’m a post-doc in the Carvajal lab at UC Davis, and am using the CODEX software V1.6.0 to call CNVs in whole exome data.  I’ve run into some possible problems I’m hoping you can help me with.
> >
> > 1. The readlength vector in the coverageObj object shows for my data a read length of 99 for all samples, but read lengths are 100.  Is this normal?
>
> This seems just to be just a boundary issue, i don't think it should affect your analyses.
> >
> > 2. The “ref” iRanges object in the bambedObj object shows BED file regions of length 1 bp longer than they should be, as if the BED file reader did not account for the fact that BED files have 0-based start and 1-based end addresses.  Is this expected behavior?
>
> Again, a boundary issue, like length(region) = end - start, rather than end-start+1. Your analyses should be fine, but Yuchao should weigh in.
> >
> > 3. This is the issue I’m mainly concerned with.  I decided to double check the raw coverage data that the CODEX coverObj object “Y” matrix showed, comparing it to coverage data we had already obtained from our data.  The values for the different regions are often fairly similar, but sometimes very different.  For example, in one region CODEX reports a raw coverage of 95 while our data show 58X average coverage per bp in that region.  I’m wondering if maybe CODEX is using a very different way of computing raw coverage?  Let me describe how we compute it.  In both CODEX and our case, a read mapping quality threshold of 20 is used.  In our case, we are computing coverage using samtools to select reads with mapping quality >= 20 and then using bedtools to compute coverage in those reads using the bedtools coverage -d command, and finally, we read the output of that command and take the mean of the reported coverage values over all base pairs of that region, yielding in this case a mean of 57.6, which we round up to 58X.
> >
>
>
> I think this has to do with how we filter based on quality score. Yuchao should weigh in.
>
> Nancy

messages.subject: Re: CODEX 1.6.0
messages.body_plain:
Thanks.  I had considered that CODEX might be reporting total number of reads, but when I looked at a pileup at an exon in a genome browser and manually counted reads, it didn’t seem to be anywhere near close.  However, it may have been that I wasn’t taking into account the map quality.  Does CODEX count a read that is partially covering an exon as a whole read, or a fractional read?

ted

messages.subject: Re: CODEX 1.6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ted,

We use Rsamtools to scan the bam and IRanges to get overlapped number of reads within the exonic regions. With this said, we coded the part below ourselves but all functions are from the Rsamtools and IRanges packages.  You might find detailed information if you look at ?countOverlaps.

Cheers,
Yuchao

        which <- RangesList(quack = IRanges(st - 10000, ed +
            10000))
        names(which) <- as.character(chr)
        what <- c("pos", "mapq", "qwidth")
        flag <- scanBamFlag(isDuplicate = FALSE, isUnmappedQuery = FALSE,
            isNotPassingQualityControls = FALSE, isFirstMateRead = TRUE)
        param <- ScanBamParam(which = which, what = what, flag = flag)
        bam <- scanBam(bamurl, param = param)[[1]]
        mapqfilter <- (bam[["mapq"]] >= mapqthres)
        readlength[i] <- round(mean(bam[["qwidth"]]))
        message("Getting coverage for sample ", sampname[i, 1],
            ": ", "read length ", readlength[i], ".", sep = "")
        irang <- IRanges(bam[["pos"]][mapqfilter], width = bam[["qwidth"]][mapqfilter])
